title: KV260 first boot from the SD card

clauses.text: the board's U-Boot finds extlinux/extlinux.conf on the card, the menu and the Linux boot text appear on the serial console (PS UART1, 115200 8N1)

steps.do: Write the card with kv260-write-sd.sh, insert it, connect the micro-USB cable and open the serial ports at 115200 8N1 (the second of the four is usually the console), then power on.
steps.expect: U-Boot scans mmc 1, finds /extlinux/extlinux.conf, the IYAKKI menu shows, the kernel starts and the IYAKKI start lines appear on the serial port.
steps.runner_did: Booted the same kernel and userspace in QEMU's virt machine (the ZynqMP machine model does not start on this QEMU); not the board's firmware

clauses.text: Ethernet comes up and gets an address

steps.do: Connect the Ethernet cable before power-on and read the network line in the boot text or run iyakki hwreport.
steps.expect: eth0 has a link and an address from the router.

clauses.text: the shell is shown on the DisplayPort monitor

steps.do: Connect a DisplayPort monitor before power-on. If the screen stays black, try the menu entries 'device tree from the SD card' (rev B, then rev A) from the serial console.
steps.expect: The IYAKKI shell start screen appears on the monitor.

steps.do: Plug a USB keyboard into one of the board's USB ports and press a key in the shell.

clauses.text: shutdown and a second boot work

steps.do: Power off from the shell, power on again.
steps.expect: The second boot reaches the same screen.
